docs.purpose: Lets a signed-in admin see whether they have two-factor authentication set up, start enrolling an authenticator app, or remove two-factor from their own account.
docs.data_story: It reads 1 table — `admin_backup_codes` and writes `admin_backup_codes` and `admin_audit_log`. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 5 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `src/features/admin-security/api/useAdminSecurity.ts`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: The audit row applies only to DELETE (unenroll), which calls writeAdminAudit for 'mfa_unenrolled'. POST (start enrollment) does NOT write an audit row — the 'mfa_enrolled' event is written by .../mfa/verify instead. GET/POST talk to Supabase Auth's MFA API (listFactors/enroll), not a raw table; admin_backup_codes is the only directly queried table. All three verbs require authMethod === 'session' (403 for admin_key/dev_bypass sentinels). POST projection is {factor_id, qr_code, secret, uri}; DELETE is {unenrolled:true}; the recorded projection is the GET shape. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: FINDINGS. (1) AUDIT ASYMMETRY: only DELETE writes admin_audit_log (:138). GET and POST write none — so starting an enrollment (a security-state-changing operation that mints a TOTP secret, :82-85) leaves no audit row; only the PostHog event at :96 records it, and that is best-effort (src/lib/admin/analytics.ts:112 returns early when POSTHOG_API_KEY is unset). (2) Audit failure is deliberately swallowed at :146-149 with the reason stated at :147; the response is still 200, so the caller cannot distinguish audited from unaudited. This is a documented choice, not an accident. (3) The TOTP `secret` and `qr_code` are returned in the response body at :104-105 — intentional per the header comment at :98-100, but it means the plaintext secret transits the envelope. (4) CENSUS DISAGREEMENT: the census lists census_reads [admin_backup_codes] and census_writes [admin_backup_codes, admin_audit_log] — all confirmed — but MISSES `profiles`, which every request reads through verifyAdminAuth (src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:117-120). It also misses the conditional admin_backup_codes SELECT/UPDATE inside the MFA gate (src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:116, :127), reachable only when ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED='true'. (5) The TOTP factors themselves are NOT in this repo's Postgres — they live in Supabase GoTrue, reached via supabase.auth.mfa.* at :56, :82, :127; there is no local table for them. (6) No SELECT *. All SQL is parameterised (src/lib/admin/backup-codes.ts:73, :77, :89, :95). | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control, revalidate, dynamic or in-process cache in the file. | Other guards / classification: CSRF Origin allowlist on POST and DELETE via src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:70-78 (MUTATING_METHODS at :45, isOriginAllowed at :319-338, default-deny at :336). MFA aal2 gate at src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:143-173 — INERT unless process.env.ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED === 'true' (:143); when armed, an x-admin-backup-code header (:156) is accepted as a single-use challenge alternative (:158). | No test file under src/tests/** imports this route.
